speeches.speaker: Sid Sidebottom
speeches.brief: Detailed changes in the rural R&D bill allowing statutory research and development corporations to undertake marketing alongside industry-owned ones, requiring funding agreements between government and statutory RDCs to be in place by 1 July 2014, and streamlining board appointments by limiting selection committees to five members serving up to three years.

speeches.speaker: Sid Sidebottom
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of a further companion bill removing maximum research, development and marketing charge rate caps from the Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Act 1999, on the same basis as the companion levies bill.

speeches.speaker: Dick Adams
speeches.brief: Detailed the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill's changes across 10 acts affecting 15 research and development corporations, including new funding agreements required from July 2014 and streamlined board selection processes, and paid tribute to retiring committee colleague Alby Schultz.

speeches.speaker: Sharman Stone
speeches.brief: Supported the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill but argued New Zealand should contribute to Australian RDC marketing levies under the Closer Economic Relations agreement since its exporters benefit too, and lamented that the Tatura Research Institute, once a world leader in orchard trellis systems, now has virtually no research scientists left.
